assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators opened a whole class of quantum matter: the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall state, its observation in HgTe quantum wells, and the discovery of three-dimensional topological insulators with protected surface states. The concept is original, clear and has reshaped condensed-matter physics, materials science and quantum-device thinking.
assessment.attribution: Kane (with Mele) supplied the decisive theory of the Z2 topological insulator; Molenkamp led the first experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall effect in HgTe; Hasan led the first ARPES observation of 3D topological insulators. Mele is an equally strong co-originator of the Kane-Mele work and the cap of three forces a hard choice; theory by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and by Fu, Kane and Mele is not fully represented in the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Predictions date from 2005-2007 and experiments from 2007-2008, with many independent confirmations across materials, so the interpretation is stable and recognition is timely to somewhat overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the three-name configuration drops Mele or an experimental pioneer, and whether credit for theory outside the credited names is fairly handled.
Which experimental result (2D versus 3D) should be recognised as decisive is partly a judgment call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Detection of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos with IceCube opened neutrino astronomy at TeV-PeV energies and gave first evidence of cosmic-ray accelerators such as the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane. It is a technically bold detector concept (cubic-kilometre ice instrumentation) delivering a new window on the Universe. As an experimentalist in astroparticle instrumentation I regard this as strongly Nobel-worthy, with my own field background noted as a possible bias.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and championed the IceCube concept and led the collaboration; Karle was a leading figure in detector construction, calibration and the discovery analysis. IceCube is a large collaboration and the AMANDA and other predecessors contributed, so a one-to-three person prize is inevitably a simplification, but the credited pair is a defensible core.
assessment.maturity: Discovery of the diffuse flux in 2013 has been confirmed with multiple channels and updated analyses; source identification is progressing but not complete. The existence of the astrophysical flux is solid, so recognition is reasonably timely.
uncertainties: Individual attribution within a very large collaboration and with predecessor experiments such as AMANDA and Baikal.
Source associations (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068) are still statistically modest compared with the diffuse-flux discovery.
I have no independent verification of the exact significance figures beyond general knowledge.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, brought atomic clocks to the 1e-18 fractional uncertainty regime. It is an original and clearly defined idea with large impact on metrology, tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and the planned redefinition of the second.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated early clocks; Ye drove the experimental realisation to record accuracy and precision. The two-name configuration is clean, though trapped-ion clock work and frequency-comb contributions (already recognised in 2005) form adjacent credit.
assessment.maturity: Concept dates from 2001-2003 and multiple groups worldwide have reproduced and surpassed it; comparisons between clocks confirm it. Recognition is mature and timely.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wishes to also credit ion-clock pioneers or to treat the lattice clock separately.
Redefinition of the second has not yet occurred, so full practical impact is still pending.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Baryon acoustic oscillations provide a standard ruler imprinted in the large-scale distribution of galaxies and are one of the cornerstone probes of dark energy and the expansion history. The detection in the SDSS and 2dFGRS surveys is a clear, robust and lasting observational discovery.
assessment.attribution: The 2005 detections were made by Eisenstein and collaborators in SDSS luminous red galaxies and by Cole, Peacock and collaborators in the 2dFGRS power spectrum; the theoretical idea goes back to Peebles, Yu, Sunyaev and Zeldovich, which the supplied credit does not include. This is a large survey collaboration context with credit shared among many.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many independent surveys (BOSS, eBOSS, DESI) over two decades, with consistent results; mature and timely.
uncertainties: Historical theory credit to Peebles and others lies outside the credited names.
Recent DESI hints of evolving dark energy might change the interpretive context, though BAO as a measurement stays solid.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise clean quantum many-body models, with the Mott-insulator transition, single-site-resolved quantum gas microscopes and quantum simulation of Hubbard physics. It is original, has had broad influence and links atomic physics with condensed-matter theory.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch, Cirac and others) proposed the Bose-Hubbard realisation; Greiner and Bloch carried out the Mott-insulator experiment and developed quantum gas microscopes. Cirac, Jaksch and the Hänsch-lab contributions complicate a three-person limit.
assessment.maturity: Mott transition (2002) and microscopy (2009-2010) were broadly replicated; the field is active and mature though quantum-simulation advantage claims are still developing.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among Bloch, Greiner, Zoller, Cirac and Jaksch is contested.
Another ballot entry (B019/B031) overlaps with the same theorists, and the committee should avoid double counting.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene revealed flat bands with correlated insulating and superconducting states in a tunable two-dimensional platform, creating the field of twistronics. The idea is original and the impact has been rapid and large.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted flat bands at the magic angle in 2011; Jarillo-Herrero's group observed correlated insulators and superconductivity in 2018. The theory-plus-experiment pair is a natural prize structure, though experimental co-authors such as Cao and Fatemi contributed.
assessment.maturity: Replicated by many groups across numerous moire materials, but the microscopic mechanism of superconductivity and correlated states is still under debate, so it may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: The origin of superconductivity remains unsettled.
Whether sufficient time has passed for the committee to treat the field as stable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics established strong coupling of superconducting qubits to microwave resonators and is the architecture underpinning superconducting quantum computing, readout and control. Highly influential and clearly defined.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Wallraff and Schoelkopf with collaborators proposed (2004) and demonstrated (2004) circuit QED; theory plus two experimental leaders is a coherent three-person structure.
assessment.maturity: Replicated and extended worldwide for two decades. Timing is a concern because the 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits, so the committee may judge it too soon to recognise a neighbouring area.
uncertainties: Overlap with the recent 2025 prize in superconducting circuits may argue for delay.
Credit relative to Nakamura, Devoret, Martinis lineage and others in superconducting qubits.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first horizon-scale images of M87* and Sgr A* are a landmark of observational astrophysics, directly testing strong-field gravity and black-hole accretion physics and demonstrating global VLBI at 1.3 mm.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed imaging the black-hole shadow, Doeleman led the EHT's technical and scientific development, and Moran pioneered mm-VLBI and led early stages. The EHT is a collaboration of hundreds, so the three-person limit sharply compresses credit.
assessment.maturity: The images were obtained in 2019 and 2022 with follow-up polarimetric and multi-epoch results; confirmation is partly internal to the collaboration with limited independent replication, so it may be premature.
uncertainties: Large collaboration credit and the fairness of a three-person selection.
Independence of confirmation beyond the EHT collaboration itself.
